newsitem.title: UK: Imperial's Davis pleased with share start.
newsitem.headline: Imperial's Davis pleased with share start.

text.p: Imperial Tobacco chief executive Gareth Davis said the start of trading in the company's shares, spun off from Hanson Plc, said on Tuesday that the issue had gone well so far.
"It seems to have gone well so far -- we've been watching the screens with great interest," Davis told Reuters from the offices of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, stockbrokers to the company.
"We look forward to the rest of the day -- it will be interesting when the Americans come in," he said.
Imperial shares opened at 390p, above expectations which fixed on a range of 370 to 380p.
"So far so good, I think is the term. It's pretty early days yet," Davis said.

Asked whether he expected good demand from the U.S. later in the day, Davis said a seven-city roadshow to make presentations to institutions there had met good interest. "There seemed to be a very high degree of interest -- we were pleasantly surprised."
Imperial is the first Hanson company to be spun off in a demerger process that will split the conglomerate into four. The second to go, Millennium Chemicals, begins trading in New York on Wednesday.
Imperial shares were quoted at 392p by 0805 GMT.
